rules.accepted_credit_types: CE appropriate to the advanced practice role and population focus from Board-recognized providers (e.g. AANP, ANCC, AANA, ACNM, NAPNAP, US colleges); APRNs may use Category I CME for everything except jurisprudence/ethics
rules.alternatives: Instead of the 20 hours: achieving, maintaining or renewing the Board-recognized national certification for the APRN role and population focus during the licensing period (targeted CE still applies; certification does not replace pharmacotherapeutics, controlled substance or jurisprudence hours).

topics.who: APRNs with prescriptive authority: pharmacotherapeutics, in addition to the 20 hours
APRNs with prescriptive authority who prescribe controlled substances; in addition to the 20 + 5 hours (28 total)
APRNs with a prescriptive authority agreement authorizing opioids: 2 h each year on safe pain management and opioid/controlled substance prescribing; counts toward the 20 hours
All nurses: nursing jurisprudence and ethics, CNE only
Nurses providing direct patient care; HHSC-approved course
Nurses whose practice includes older adults
Nurses working in an ER setting, within 2 years of starting
APRNs authorized to receive Prescription Monitoring Program information: within 1 year of initial licensure (prescribing and monitoring controlled substances)

rules.notes: The 20 APRN hours also satisfy the RN renewal (not in addition). Prescribers of controlled substances need 28 hours in total. CE on tick-borne diseases is encouraged (not required) for APRNs treating them.
